sections.h2: Selling a house in Upper Merion
sections.html:
Upper Merion is a Montgomery County township of about 17 square miles with an estimated 36,674 residents, and it does not require a use and occupancy permit when a single-family home changes hands. What remains is the standard Pennsylvania sequence: disclosure form, agreement of sale, transfer tax, deed recording and tax proration.

The township sits about 16 miles from Philadelphia and takes in the villages of Gulph Mills, King of Prussia, Swedeland and Swedesburg, plus parts of Radnor and Wayne. A house in Swedesburg and a house near the King of Prussia mall draw different buyers, so the first job is matching your street to the right pool of buyers and the right sale route.

Upper Merion works as an employment center as much as a bedroom suburb, so many buyers want a short commute rather than a large yard. The Schuylkill River forms its northern and eastern edge, Valley Forge National Historical Park fills most of the western end, and the King of Prussia retail and office district sits in the middle.

sections.h2: No use and occupancy permit at sale
sections.html:
The township's residential permit rules require no Use and Occupancy Permit for a change of ownership of a single-family dwelling, as long as the use of the dwelling stays the same. Converting a house into a different use is a separate question for the township.

Permits still matter if you did work on the house. Buyers' inspectors and lenders ask about decks, finished basements, sheds, pools and replaced roofs. Pull your own records before you list:

  • Permit review takes up to 15 business days, and inspections need 24 hours' notice, so finishing open work before listing takes weeks, not days.
  • Residential contractors must be registered with the State and list a Pennsylvania HIC number and a certificate of insurance on the application.
  • Accessory structures have setbacks by zoning district. In R-1 and R-1A a shed or pool sits 10 feet from the side and rear lines, while R-2 and R-3 require four feet from the side and five feet from the rear.

Call the township's safety and code enforcement office if you cannot tell which zoning district your lot is in.

Public school students attend the Upper Merion Area School District. Children start at one of five K-4 elementary schools: Bridgeport, Caley Road, Candlebrook, Gulph and Roberts. They move on to Upper Merion Area Middle School for grades 5 through 8 and Upper Merion Area High School for grades 9 through 12. Mother Teresa Regional Catholic School is the parochial option.

Because the elementary school assignment depends on your street, confirm it with the district before you put a school name in your listing.

sections.h2: What do I pay and file when I sell?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the value of the real estate. The full transfer tax is usually described as 2 percent, with 1 percent to the state and 1 percent to the municipality and school district, and buyers and sellers commonly split it. Ask the Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds to confirm the rate that applies to your township and school district before you sign.

The seller's disclosure duty comes from 68 Pa.C.S. Section 7303. You complete the property disclosure statement and deliver a signed, dated copy to the buyer before the agreement of sale is signed. The form covers the roof, basement, plumbing, wiring, storm water facilities, hazardous substances and flood risk indicators. The Schuylkill runs along two edges of Upper Merion and annual precipitation runs near 48.5 inches, so answer the water questions with care. Act 74 of 2026 amended the land item and added a flood-insurance notice to the chapter.

If property taxes are behind, the Montgomery County Tax Claim Bureau holds upset sales each September and December for parcels with taxes unpaid from two years earlier, and buyers at those sales take the property subject to liens. Check with the Board of Assessment Appeals for the annual appeal deadline and forms.

At the closing table the title agent totals your mortgage payoff, the transfer tax, any unpaid taxes and prorated tax for the year. You sign the deed, and the agent sends it to the Recorder of Deeds. Ask for a net sheet ahead of time so no line item surprises you.

If the house has unpermitted work, disclose what you know on the form. Many owners apply for a permit on open work before listing, since a buyer's inspector will notice a deck or finished basement and the lender may ask about it.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits an Upper Merion house best?
sections.html:
The right route depends on how much time and repair money you have. A listing can reach the large employee pool around King of Prussia but brings showings, inspection requests and a financing timeline. A private sale saves an agent's fee and adds legal and marketing work. A direct sale to an as-is buyer shortens the schedule and removes repair negotiations, usually at a lower price.

  • Ask every buyer for proof of funds and a written closing date.
  • Request a net sheet that shows transfer tax, payoff, tax proration and any repair credits.
  • Compare the net figure from each route, not the headline price.

faqs.q: Is a certificate needed to sell a house in Upper Merion Township?
faqs.a: Not for a single-family home whose use stays the same. No use and occupancy permit is required for the change of ownership. Ask the township office first for a multi-unit or non-residential property.

faqs.q: What is a typical home value in Upper Merion?
faqs.a: Owners report a middle home value of $455,300. Your house will price off nearby sales, so ask an agent or appraiser for comparable sales on your street.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax when an Upper Merion house sells?
faqs.a: The law does not assign it. Most sale agreements split it between buyer and seller, and the buyer is responsible if the amount paid is questioned. Put the split in writing in your agreement of sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Upper Merion house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but disclose what you know. Pennsylvania's disclosure form asks about additions, remodeling and structural changes, and a seller cannot make statements the seller knows are false. Many owners apply for a permit on the open work before listing.

faqs.q: How quickly can a cash sale close in Upper Merion?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close as fast as the title search, the deed and the transfer tax paperwork allow, because no lender is involved. The timeline is set in the agreement of sale, so ask the buyer for a written date and what must happen before it.
